patch_resolves_note: The staged patch.diff does not apply cleanly to the vulnerable workspace checkout, so fixed-side validation used the authoritative n132/arvo:33556-fix image with the same fixed-side instrumentation patch. In that image the original PoC guards the copy event, and the nearest accepted boundary case (4095-byte copy span) reaches the copy with the required predicate satisfied.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

nodes.description: First project-side parse/materialization of the attacker buffer: `parse_new_conf_line()` splits the single input line at the first `=` and stores a `new_config_item` whose key is `lxc.rootfs.options` and whose value is the long attacker-controlled options string later searched for `idmap=`.

The caller computes the distance from `p2` to the next comma and passes that attacker-derived span as `strlcpy()`'s `size` argument, even though the destination is `opts->userns_path[PATH_MAX]`; the bounds check only executes after the call returns.

ASan crash site. `strlcpy()` interprets the caller-supplied 5677 as destination capacity, computes a 5676-byte copy, and writes past `rootfs->mnt_opts.userns_path` inside the heap `lxc_conf` allocation.

edges.description: The same computed idmap-path span is carried unchanged from the comma-search checkpoint to the ensuing copy call into opts->userns_path.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records idmap_span_check.copy_span_bytes == userns_path_copy.copy_span_bytes == 5677.
